target_scope.rules_scope: English base game, 6–12 players, source identified in the supplied materials as English Rules 2.0 (2016)
target_scope.scope_caution: The visible English booklet has a 2016 copyright and S&D 0062 code; no visible Rules 2.0 revision label was found on its eight pages. The 2.0 identity is supplied by the task/input descriptor, not independently established by a printed revision line.

isolation.read_only_inputs: Only the original English PDF/OCR/pages, two specified recovered raw manuals/pages, and frozen benchmark-v2 questions and keys were read. No canonical summary, summary snapshots, reader outputs/prompts, grades, earlier reviews, research notes, parent history, browser summaries, or desired-result claims were used.
isolation.method: All 8 English, 8 Polish and 4 Chinese supplied page images visually inspected, including complete credits; PDF page counts/metadata and embedded text also inspected. Embedded text extraction is damaged or incomplete, especially the Polish repeated example text on noncorresponding pages, so visible page images control. Language comparisons are reviewer paraphrases, not a certified translation.
isolation.quotation_policy: No source prose is quoted verbatim in this review; proper names and card/rule labels identify sources and mechanics.

sources.authority: Strong internal evidence of a publisher-produced Traditional Chinese localization: GoKids/Smirk branding, original creators and dual 2016 rights credits, matching base-game contents. A primary rulebook for its own localization.
sources.licensing_assessment: The credits assert original and local rights, but contain no explicit cross-edition erratum declaration or guarantee of English 2.0 equivalence. No host/download provenance was inferred because browsing and outside research were excluded.
sources.applicability_limit: The four PDF sheets arrange two booklet panels each; page references in this review use PDF sheet numbers. The localization closely corroborates English procedures, including the same unspecific tied-player Showdown instruction on p2. It supplies no explicit multiway tied-leader mechanism and cannot independently establish that all Polish additions are common original rules.

new_primary_information.procedure: Three or more qualifying leaders tied for highest total
new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p4 explicitly instructs further normal rounds until there is one winner or only two tied players remain; the remaining pair then uses the extra two-player payout procedure.
new_primary_information.classification: Version-specific explicit executable addition; not an established English 2.0 clarification
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p4 directs tied players to another Showdown but supplies only two-player equipment/procedures. Chinese p2 repeats the general tied-player Showdown direction without this normal-round fallback.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: No manual states that this Polish addition is an original-designer/publisher erratum binding the 2016 English edition. Shared copyright, component identity and a later file date are insufficient to establish that.

new_primary_information.procedure: An outsider can win after double Steal in a two-way endgame tiebreak
new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p4 explicitly notes that the compensation bar awarded to nonparticipants can make a player outside the tied pair the winner.
new_primary_information.classification: Localized explicit corroboration of an already defensible English cross-rule inference
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p4 uses a table-wide sole-highest condition and p8 gives one bar to every nonfinalist after double Steal; neither contains this explicit combined example.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: English Q27 can be supported from English rules as an inference; Polish wording increases interpretive confidence but is not needed as an English erratum.

new_primary_information.procedure: Ambush retaliation when the only voter against the ambusher already died as a Target
new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p6 explains the illustrated Red/Yellow/Pink case: Yellow is already eliminated, so Red’s retaliation removes no additional live player.
new_primary_information.classification: Localized elaboration of an outcome already explicitly shown in English p6
new_primary_information.english_comparison: The English example already leaves Red and Pink alive and restricts Red to its own voter, Yellow.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: Safe to paraphrase as an inference/explanation of the existing English example; not a new exception authorizing arbitrary targets.

new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p8 expressly states that every round begins with four central bars in its explanation of double Grab replenishment.
new_primary_information.classification: Localized explicit corroboration of normal English setup/round-structure inference
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p3 explicitly sets up four initial hidden bars, p4 makes four available per round and p8 names retained-pot exceptions. Ordinary empty-pot refill is not separately commanded.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: The English operational conclusion is strong but should be labeled derived. The Polish wording does not supply an English revision identifier.

new_primary_information.procedure: Gold-deck shuffle and specific physical draw instructions
new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p3 explicitly shuffles the Gold Bar deck before setup and Polish pp4,8 use top-of-deck wording for certain awards.
new_primary_information.classification: Localized setup/logistics wording additional to the English text
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p3 specifies a face-down deck and hidden-value initial pot but does not expressly command a shuffle; p4 and p8 say awards come from the deck.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: Do not add a claimed English 2.0 mandatory shuffle solely from this translation. An explicitly labeled Polish-edition procedure can include it.

new_primary_information.procedure: Showdown negotiation timing and vote-change cutoff
new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p8 caps Showdown discussion at thirty seconds. Polish p5 expressly closes vote changes once any card has been revealed.
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p8 allows a moment for discussion without a numeric cap. English p5 permits vote changes until reveal and calls for simultaneous reveal, without discussing an early single reveal.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: The thirty-second limit is absent from English scope and should not be imported. The first-reveal cutoff is a compatible local interpretation, not a newly proved universal English rule.

new_primary_information.new_information: Polish p3 adds a named-film/most-recent-viewer role and that role assigns character identities; the introductory fiction is also rethemed.
new_primary_information.english_comparison: English p3 lets players take an ID and makes no such assignment procedure mandatory.
new_primary_information.authority_limit: This difference is evidence against treating every Polish extra sentence as omitted English text. Exclude it from English Rules 2.0 additions.

reviews.independent_judgment: English p3 says each player stands a visible ID, gets its matching voting set, removes unused colors, and deals four central face-down bars from a face-down deck. Its component list identifies the own-color card as Ambush; retaining that card follows from the stated set contents.
English p5 has no turn order, permits changes until reveal, and requires simultaneous reveal after everyone places a choice.
English p5 uses the greatest count, not an absolute majority. Three exceeds two and two; Red is the only Target.

English p5 eliminates all tied highest Targets and voters who chose no Target. The p6 example expressly permits survival through voting for either tied Target. A Target is still eliminated despite having voted correctly.
Survival requires voting for a Target unless successful Ambush supplies the exception. Receiving no votes does not exempt Green from the wrong-vote elimination.

The exact three-player English p6 example gives Red and Yellow one vote each; Ambush contributes no vote. Yellow is eliminated and Pink survives by voting for Yellow. Red survives and its only retaliation-eligible voter is Yellow, already eliminated. No additional survivor dies.
reviews.qualification_or_proposed_change: The key is correct. For procedural clarity it may say that retaliation against already eliminated Yellow changes nothing; Polish p6 makes that explanation explicit, while the English example already establishes the same outcome.

reviews.independent_judgment: English p6 protects a targeted ambusher and restricts retaliation to one player who voted for that ambusher. It does not authorize killing every voter or choosing another target-color voter.
An untargeted Ambush eliminates its user under English p6.

English p4 defines a round as multiple votes with only one-, two-, or zero-survivor endings. English p5 keeps surviving IDs upright for the next vote. Four survivors therefore conspire and vote again without a payout.
English p4 awards the sole survivor all four central cards. English pp3 and8 distinguish 3-,4-,5-point values from card count.
English pp7–8 require the final two to take the three distinct Showdown choices, discuss intentions, choose face down, and reveal together.

English p4 explicitly awards one deck bar to each person outside the final vote when that vote leaves no survivors. Final-vote participants get no bar, the central four remain, and no new central gold is added.
The English p8 chart awards two central bars to each Share player.
The English p8 chart awards zero to Share and four to Steal.
The English p8 chart awards one to Grab One & Go and three to Steal.
The English p8 chart awards one to Grab One & Go and three to Share.
The English p8 double-Grab chart and accompanying note give one each, retain two, and add only two new central bars next round.
The English p8 double-Steal chart and note give neither finalist a bar, give each other player one from the deck, and retain the central pot.

English p4 sets 25 points for 6–9 players, 24 for 10–12, and highest total among multiple qualifiers. English p8 checks after round-end payouts. At least the threshold suffices, rather than an exact total.

For exactly two tied leaders, English p4 directs another Showdown and continues until one player anywhere has the highest gold total. English p8 returns all players and IDs to the next normal round if nobody has won.
reviews.qualification_or_proposed_change: Correct as an account of the printed tie instruction. The booklet does not separately spell out how to supply a fresh four-bar pot for repeated endgame Showdowns after the preceding payout exhausted it. Do not treat this answer as a complete specification of that setup detail.

reviews.independent_judgment: English p4 permits any covert/overt communication, explicitly including texts and showing cards, for roughly at most ninety seconds. English p5 delegates the call for final choices to the owner.
English p5 says choose the intended victim’s matching card, put it face down in front of oneself, or substitute Ambush if suspecting attack. English p3 identifies Ambush as the own-color card.
English p5 knocks down eliminated IDs and retains standing survivor IDs for the next vote. English p8 resets all at the next normal round.

The four-card pool is explicit at initial setup (p3), is available each round (p4), and is retained or partly replenished in the specific exceptions (pp4,8). Dealing four fresh hidden cards after an empty pot is the coherent normal-round inference. There is no standalone English sentence explicitly directing that ordinary refill.
reviews.qualification_or_proposed_change: Revise support labeling, not the inferred payout: describe dealing four new hidden bars as an inference from the per-round four-bar pool and exception notes. Polish p8 expressly says each round begins with four central bars, but this is localized corroboration, not proof of an English 2.0 erratum.

reviews.independent_judgment: English p7 expressly keeps Blue as the highest-count Target even when Blue survives Ambush. Votes for Purple still fail the survival test; no retally or promotion occurs. Blue chooses one Blue voter for retaliation.

English p4 orders tied players to another Showdown, but pp3,7–8 supply only two sets of cards and a two-player procedure. Nothing in the original eight pages arranges three or more tied leaders. The key correctly identifies the unresolved arrangement.
reviews.qualification_or_proposed_change: Keep the English-source limitation. An explicitly separate Polish-file-2017 rule could describe additional normal rounds until a sole winner or a two-way tie remains. Do not replace the frozen English key with that rule without changing its declared source/version scope.

reviews.independent_judgment: English p8 gives every nonfinalist one deck bar after double Steal, and English p4 permits any single player at the table to become highest during tie resolution. Applying those instructions together permits an outside player to win if that award makes them the sole highest qualifier.
reviews.qualification_or_proposed_change: This is an inference from the English rules, not an explicit English worked example. Polish p4 explicitly describes an outside player winning after the tied pair both Steal; that corroborates the interpretation for its own localization. The extra-Showdown pot setup detail remains underdefined.

frozen_key_review.overall: No reviewed key directly contradicts an explicit English rule or diagram. Q09, Q24 and Q27 rely on structural/cross-rule inference to differing degrees; Q24 should not be represented as an explicit English refill sentence. Q26 correctly exposes an unresolved English procedure, rather than resolving it. Correct keys and corroborating translations do not establish complete procedural coverage.

proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.target: English Rules 2.0 source-support annotation for Q24
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.proposal: Retain the inferred four-new-hidden-bars answer, but identify it as derived from English pp3,4,8; optionally cite Polish-file-2017 p8 separately as localization corroboration.
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.why: Avoids upgrading an inference or foreign-language sentence into an express English rule.

proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.target: English Rules 2.0 source-support annotation for Q27
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.proposal: Retain the outsider-wins result as a combined inference from English pp4,8; identify the explicit Polish p4 worked condition as corroboration belonging to Polish-file-2017.
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.why: The conclusion is well supported, but the English source does not give the combined scenario verbatim.

proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.target: Optional separately scoped Polish-file-2017 clarification appendix; not the frozen English bank
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.proposal: State that the Polish manual resolves a three-or-more-way qualifying tie with further normal rounds until a sole winner or exactly two tied leaders remain, then uses an extra two-player payout. Label it as a Polish localization procedure, pending evidence that it applies to the 2016 English edition.
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.why: The new primary manual contains a concrete executable branch, but cross-edition authority is not established.

proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.proposal: Explain that Yellow is already eliminated, so Red cannot remove an additional live player in the illustrated case.
proposed_explicitly_versioned_changes.why: The English outcome already entails this; Polish p6 only expands the explanation.

unresolved_gaps.case: Three or more qualifying players tied for highest point total
unresolved_gaps.english_missing: How to arrange and execute a tiebreak using only the printed two-player Showdown mechanism.
unresolved_gaps.new_manual_effect: Polish p4 supplies a normal-round fallback for its edition. Chinese p2 does not.
unresolved_gaps.resolution_status: Unresolved for the frozen English Rules 2.0 scope; locally resolved only under the explicitly identified Polish manual.
unresolved_gaps.needed_evidence: An English erratum/FAQ or a designer/original publisher statement explicitly applying the multiway mechanism to this English edition, or an openly authorized change of rules scope.

unresolved_gaps.case: All remaining participants choose Ambush, leaving no counted target votes
unresolved_gaps.english_missing: Whether zero votes makes anybody a Target, whether all Ambushes fail, or whether a vote is repeated. Highest-count language and the exclusion of Ambush from the count do not explicitly resolve this zero-count boundary.
unresolved_gaps.new_manual_effect: Polish p6 and Chinese p3 repeat that Ambush is not a vote and that a nontarget ambusher dies; neither supplies an explicit all-Ambush/zero-count ruling.
unresolved_gaps.resolution_status: Unresolved across all three inspected manuals. All ambushers dying is a plausible reading, not a newly verified explicit ruling.
unresolved_gaps.needed_evidence: A primary ruling for a vote containing no counted target selections.

unresolved_gaps.case: Another endgame Showdown is required after the preceding Showdown distributed all central gold
unresolved_gaps.english_missing: A standalone setup/refill instruction for the extra Showdown, including fresh pot supply after a consumed pot. The natural repeat-the-four-bar-procedure reading is strong but implicit.
unresolved_gaps.new_manual_effect: Polish p4 explicitly repeats extra two-way payouts and p8 supplies the ordinary four-bar-per-round principle, but does not independently state fresh-pot handling specifically for repeated extra Showdowns. Chinese likewise supplies no special setup paragraph.
unresolved_gaps.resolution_status: No directly explicit special-case setup in the inspected materials. Distinguish this physical procedure omission from the clearly stated requirement to hold another two-player Showdown.
unresolved_gaps.needed_evidence: A primary clarification that extra endgame Showdowns use a newly prepared four-bar pot when the preceding pot was consumed, and how any retained pot is handled.

unresolved_gaps.case: The Gold Bar deck has too few cards for a multi-player compensation payout
unresolved_gaps.english_missing: No shortage, replacement, partial-award priority or emergency scoring procedure is printed. Finite 80-card contents and simultaneous awards do not themselves define one.
unresolved_gaps.new_manual_effect: Neither recovered manual adds a deck-exhaustion rule.
unresolved_gaps.resolution_status: Unsourced if reached; no claim that this review has established an actually reachable legal play sequence. This is a conditional resource-completeness concern, distinct from the established three-way-tie gap.
unresolved_gaps.needed_evidence: Either a proof the case is unreachable under the 6–12-player winning checks, or an applicable primary shortage ruling.

secondary_underdefinition_not_counted_as.case: Order/selection of hidden Gold Bar cards during split awards and ordinary refill
secondary_underdefinition_not_counted_as.assessment: The manuals specify card counts and hidden initial values, but not a full physical dealing protocol for unequal individual card values. A neutral hidden draw/deal is conventional. Do not fabricate an official priority rule; this is lower-level logistics rather than evidence contradicting a payout key.

conclusion.scope_identity: Both recovered files are strongly evidenced localizations of the same base game; neither is proven textually or revision-identical to English Rules 2.0.
conclusion.applicable_authoritative_clarifications: No newly added translated-only procedure has been established as a binding correction to the target English edition. Shared-rule explanations can corroborate conclusions independently supported by the original English pages.
conclusion.key_result: All 27 keys individually reviewed. No direct explicit-English contradiction found; distinguish inference support and printed limitations.
conclusion.completeness_result: No PASS or presumed gap resolution. The English multiway tie branch remains materially unresolved, and the inspected manuals do not explicitly settle a zero-count all-Ambush vote. The Polish manual offers a useful, precisely attributable multiway procedure only for its own presently evidenced scope.
